chunks: From him, from al-Naḍr, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Wallād Ḥafṣ ibn Sālim, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the taslim in the two rakʿahs of al-watr. He said: Yes. So if you have a need, then go out and fulfill it, then return and perform one rakʿah.

key_terms.اقْضِهَا: fulfill it or attend to it
key_terms.الْوَتْرِ: the odd-numbered prayer unit, here referring to the final part of the night prayer
key_terms.حَاجَةٌ: a need or matter requiring attention

ai.seo_question: Can the two rakʿahs of al-shafʿ be separated from the one rakʿah of al-watr with taslim?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of separating the two rakʿahs of al-shafʿ from the single rakʿah of al-watr with taslim. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام affirms this separation and indicates that one may attend to a need in between and then return to perform the final rakʿah.
